operative_text.controlling:
3.29   If a statement of claim is served within an extension of time
for service permitted by the Court under rule 3.26 or rule 3.27,
when it is served the statement of claim must be accompanied with
(a) a copy of the order granting the extension, or
(b) written notice of the order.

BOOK_B.title: Notice of extension of time for service

commentary.text: Rule 3.29 See Alberta Rules of Court, Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 3.29. The respondents also argue that the renewed statement of claim was not endorsed by the clerk of the court, as required by rule 11(7). Is the unendorsed renewed statement of claim a nullity or a curable irregularity? . . . . . Rule 558 reflects the judicial reluctance to treat procedural defects as nullities that halt proceedings… . . . . . In this case, a renewal order was properly granted by the master. While an endorsement helps identify that the proper procedural step has been taken, the lack of endorsement does not negate the fact that the order for renewal was granted. Therefore, an unendorsed renewed statement of claim is not a nullity that halts a proceeding, but a curable irregularity. When can a curable irregularity be cured? Under rule 558, the court must consider whether the noncompliance with the Rules can be cured without prejudice to the other party. Oberg v. Foothills Provincial General Hospital (1999), 232 A.R. 263 (C.A.), at 269, per Conrad J.A.
